acceptanceCriteria: The spec records the unit-level frontier design with numbered requirements, failure modes and rollback before implementation.

A plan whose changed root packages are not imported, directly or transitively, by any open nested module carries no nested-module unknown; a plan that changes such a package keeps it, naming the nested module.
An unreadable nested module or import graph keeps the plan-level frontier open (fail closed).
Replays of PRs 571, 614, 594, 557 and 610 report before/after unknowns and selections with zero new misses.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Found by the V1-0867 lane (branch claude/v1-0867-nested-frontier, d5128a48, base 3dc863bd). V1-0867 (AFP-V0-028) closes the go:nested-module-frontier only when no nested module can reach the root. In this repository tools/local-authority requires and replaces the root module (github.com/Beamfall/corvint => ../..), so every Go plan stays scope UNKNOWN on that frontier, even when the change touches no package local-authority imports. Its imports are internal/authoritystore, internal/localauthority and internal/cem/... Moving the frontier to unit level, attached to the root packages that an open nested module imports directly or transitively, would drop the unknown for most plans. This is a reachability design change that needs a spec decision.
title: affected: attach an open nested-module frontier to the root packages it imports instead of the whole plan
